title: ALMA Observations of HD 141569’s Circumstellar Disk
question: What are the dust and CO gas structure, kinematics and masses of the HD141569 disk, and is the gas primordial or second-generation (debris-related)?

what.value: Previous continuum/total-system flux densities (Keck, IRAS, HST, APEX, JCMT) in Table 1

evidence.quote: Summary of select previous HD 141569 debris disk observations.

external_data.citation: Fisher 2000; Walker 1988; Marsh 2002; Mouillet 2001; Augereau 1999; Nilsson 2010; Sylvester 2001

what.value: CARMA CO(1-0) flux 1.6 ± 0.2 Jy km/s and gas mass 13 (+50/-9) Earth masses, SMA 870um flux 8.2 ± 2.4 mJy

evidence.quote: The (cite: flaherty) CARMA observations found an integrated line flux for CO(1-0) of $1.6\pm 0.2\rm~Jy~km~s^{-1}$
The re-analyzed *Hipparcos* Catalog distance with 1-$\sigma$ uncertainty is $116\pm8$ pc (cite: van).

what.value: CO spectroscopic data (A32, Be) from Splatalogue

evidence.quote: The spectral information for the CO molecule was obtained from the Splatalogue database

recipe.method: CASA calibration with WVR, Tsys, bandpass, flux, phase; flag antenna 14 and 120 bad channels in SPW 1 and 3; split

recipe.goal: Image continuum and fit uniform disk to visibilities
recipe.method: CLEAN image of line-free data; uvmodelfit uniform disk with chi^2 minimization
assumptions: Flux uncertainty dominated by 10% absolute flux scale

recipe.goal: Make CO moment and channel maps and measure line flux
recipe.method: uvcontsub, zeroth/first moments; flux from summing zeroth moment above 3 sigma times number of beams
key_parameters: channel spacing 0.5 km/s for channel maps

recipe.goal: Fit Keplerian disk model to CO velocity field
recipe.method: Uniform Keplerian disk projected, convolved with beam, compared to first moment map in image domain
key_parameters: 3 chains, 100 thousand links each, ~1000 burn-in; sigma = 0.5 km/s
assumptions: No inner cavity, temperature profile or line broadening in model

recipe.goal: Estimate mm dust and debris masses
recipe.method: Optically thin single-size grain ring estimate; then 100-ring collisional cascade model 10-50 au, r^-1 surface density, s<50 km, matched to 3.8 mJy
key_parameters: grain density 2.5 g/cm3, size 1 mm, T_star 10500 K, size distribution M_s ∝ s^-0.5
assumptions: Black-body grains, albedo 0, emissivity 1 (Q_nu=2s/lambda for large wavelengths); kappa=3 cm2/g equivalent

recipe.method: Optically thin LTE CO(3-2) mass from integrated flux with partition function
key_parameters: T = 33 K; A32 = 2.497e-6 Hz; Be = 57.635; distance 116 pc
assumptions: Optically thin, LTE; H2/CO = 1e4 for total gas

answer_key.quantity: mm grain mass lower limit (R=10 au)

evidence.quote: which yields a mm grain mass[^3] of $0.04~\rm M_{\oplus}$

not_stated_but_needed: Number of clean iterations and mask used for CLEAN; image size and cell size
Which channels were treated as CO-free for the continuum and uvcontsub fit order
Velocity-axis reference/ rest frequency used for moment maps; moment-map clipping thresholds
How the first moment map was sampled (pixels, masking) for chi^2 and how the model was projected
Details on how the 1/32 flagged channels were chosen
Phase calibrator and gain solution intervals
Treatment of correlated noise between moment-map pixels in chi^2
missing_for_reproduction: moment-map thresholds and flagged channel ranges
score_reason: Data public and recipe fairly simple with numeric results, but imaging and MCMC details and code are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, simple analysis with numeric tabulated results (flux, CO flux, Keplerian parameters).
